text: Declaration of agriculture as a state profession, promotion of organic farming, and ensuring fair pricing and welfare for farmers.
Provision of financial security, crop insurance, and pension schemes for farmers over sixty years of age.
Strategic management of water bodies, increasing storage capacity, rejuvenating rivers, and achieving state-wide water self-sufficiency.
Provision of pure drinking water as a basic right for all citizens for free, including a ban on the commercial sale of water.
Revitalizing trader welfare boards, providing interest-free loans, and protecting small traders from multinational dominance.
Improving public transport infrastructure, safety standards, and connectivity across the state.
Economic vision based on self-sufficiency, localized resource management, and regional sustainability.
Focus on industrial development in rural and semi-urban areas to prevent urban migration.
Promotion of eco-friendly and sustainable industries aligned with environmental protection.
Protection of the rights, job security, and working conditions of employees in the information technology sector.
Shifting the state energy grid towards renewable sources such as solar and wind power.
Development of spiritual, historical, and eco-tourism while preserving local culture and traditions.
Reform of the education system to prioritize mother-tongue instruction and skill-based, vocational learning.
Environmental conservation initiatives and implementation of massive afforestation programs across the state.
Expansion of forest cover and protection of biodiversity through the planting of indigenous tree species.
Policies ensuring the rights and protection of wildlife and domestic animals.
Implementation of scientific and sustainable methods for solid and liquid waste disposal.
Strategies to mitigate and adapt to the global impacts of climate change within the regional context.
Strict regulation of sand mining and mineral extractions to prevent ecological damage and resource depletion.
